info.title: chat-v1
info.description: The participant-facing messaging protocol for resident agents (docs/chat-v1-plan.md). JSON-RPC 2.0 over WebSocket at /ws/chat, authenticated by a signed token from /api/ws-token (?token=) or a raw bridge key (OMNI_CHAT_BRIDGE_KEYS). Source of truth for the signatures is the ChatMethodMap in src/shared/types.ts; a parity test keeps this document's method names aligned. Governance follows gui-v1's rules: additive-only once stable; clients tolerate unknown notification methods and unknown enum values. There is no replay buffer: message ids are monotonic and durable, so clients resume with chat.list_messages({after: lastSeenId}) and dedupe live notifications by id. Message `from` ids follow the participant grammar: `user` (the collective human), `human:<principalId>` (named cloud team member), `ext:<network>:<id>` (bridged external user), `system`, else a bare agent roster id.

methods.name: chat.hello
methods.summary: Handshake: the caller's stamped participant identity and server capabilities.

methods.name: chat.list_channels
methods.summary: Every channel the caller can see: #team, named channels, DM threads, #system.

methods.name: chat.list_messages
methods.summary: Keyset page of the durable log, ascending id order. `after` pages forward (resume/replay); `before` or neither returns the newest window.

methods.name: chat.post_message
methods.summary: Post to a named channel or a human↔agent DM. The ONLY write; the server alone decides which agents wake. Identity comes from authentication — bridge connections must pass asExternal, nobody else may. DM threads come in two shapes: the collective `dm:user:<agent>` thread is every human's; a personal thread (`dm:<human:pid|ext:...>~<agent>`) is team-VISIBLE but single-writer — only its named participant may post into it.

params.name: replyTo
params.description: Threads under this message's root (named channels only).

params.name: asExternal
params.description: Bridge scope only: post as a bridged external user (stamped ext:<network>:<id>).

methods.name: chat.create_channel
methods.summary: Create a named channel; the id slug derives from the name and is fixed at creation.

methods.name: chat.update_channel
methods.summary: Edit a named channel's description (blank clears it). Built-ins refuse.

methods.name: chat.delete_channel
methods.summary: Delete a named channel and its message history. Built-ins refuse.

methods.name: chat.set_channel_members
methods.summary: Replace a named channel's member list (agent roster ids); null restores the open state.

methods.name: chat.list_roster
methods.summary: The agent roster, projected for addressing/display (persona/config stay on the admin surface).

methods.name: chat.get_presence
methods.summary: Live runtime snapshot per agent id (state, read watermark, queued ids). Then rely on chat.presence_changed pushes.

methods.name: chat.wake_agent
methods.summary: Manually wake an agent now (WAKE_NOW, bypasses digests).

methods.name: chat.attach_agent_session
methods.summary: Wake the agent's process if parked and return a gui-v1 connection to its live day session (the rich-client session view).

methods.name: chat.message_added
methods.summary: Server→client: a message landed in the log (any author — humans, agents, system rows).

methods.name: chat.channel_changed
methods.summary: Server→client: a channel was created/updated (carries the channel) or deleted (carries deletedId; its rows are gone).

methods.name: chat.presence_changed
methods.summary: Server→client: the full presence snapshot (roster scale is small; full-replace is trivial to apply).

methods.name: chat.attention
methods.summary: Server→client: an agent incident (failed delivery/reflection) — also mirrored as a #system row, so the log stays the full record.

dmParticipants.description: DM channels only. Ids follow the participant grammar; channel ids use `dm:<a>:<b>` for legacy colon-free pairs and `dm:<a>~<b>` when a participant id is namespaced.

from.description: Participant id (see the grammar in info.description).

fromName.description: Display name at post time, when one is known. Absent for the collective user — self-rendering is the viewer's judgment.

replyTo.description: Thread ROOT id, pre-normalized on write (threads are one level deep).

seenMessageId.description: Read watermark: log ids at or below it have reached the agent's context.

queuedMessageIds.description: Routed but not yet delivered — will read.
